## `sf data360 activation-target create`

Create an activation target.

Creates a target with maxFileSize from 1 through 500 MB.

### Flags

| Flag                          | Required | Description                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--api-version=<value>`       | no       | Override the api version used for api requests made by this command |
| `--file=<value>` (`-f`)       | yes      | Input file path, or - to read from stdin.                           |
| `--flags-dir=<value>`         | no       | Import flag values from a directory.                                |
| `--json`                      | no       | Format output as json.                                              |
| `--target-org=<value>` (`-o`) | yes      | Username or alias of the target org.                                |
| `--timing`                    | no       | Write request timing details to stderr.                             |

### Examples

- Create from a file:

  ```shell
  sf data360 activation-target create --target-org my-org --file target.json
  ```

- Read stdin:

  ```shell
  sf data360 activation-target create --target-org my-org --file - < target.json
  ```

## `sf data360 api request`

Send a raw authenticated Data 360 API request.

Call a core-org or Direct tenant Data 360 endpoint and write the response body to stdout without a JSON envelope. POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE require explicit confirmation.

### Arguments

| Argument   | Required | Description                                   |
| ---------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `endpoint` | yes      | Relative SSOT or absolute /services endpoint. |

### Flags

| Flag                              | Required | Description                                                                 |
| --------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--api-version=<value>`           | no       | Override the api version used for api requests made by this command         |
| `--body=<value>` (`-b`)           | no       | Literal body, `@file`, or `-` for stdin.                                    |
| `--direct`                        | no       | Send the request to the Data 360 tenant API.                                |
| `--flags-dir=<value>`             | no       | Import flag values from a directory.                                        |
| `--header=<value>` (`-H`)         | no       | Request header in `name:value` format; repeat for multiple headers.         |
| `--include` (`-i`)                | no       | Include response status and headers.                                        |
| `--method=<value>` (`-X`)         | no       | HTTP request method.                                                        |
| `--no-prompt`                     | no       | Do not prompt for confirmation.                                             |
| `--no-token-cache`                | no       | Exchange a new Direct API token without reading or writing the token cache. |
| `--stream-to-file=<value>` (`-S`) | no       | Write response bytes atomically to a file.                                  |
| `--target-org=<value>` (`-o`)     | yes      | Username or alias of the target org.                                        |
| `--timing`                        | no       | Write request timing details to stderr.                                     |

### Examples

- Fetch one segment page:

  ```shell
  sf data360 api request 'segments?batchSize=1' --target-org my-org
  ```

- Submit a JSON payload from a file and include response headers:

  ```shell
  sf data360 api request connections --method POST --body @connection.json --include --target-org my-org
  ```

- Fetch Direct API metadata with an exchanged tenant token:

  ```shell
  sf data360 api request metadata --direct --target-org my-org
  ```

## `sf data360 data-kit available`

List components available to Data 360 data kits.

List components from the data-kit available-components endpoint for a required data-kit developer name. Filter by supported component type and page with the API's 1-through-200 limit and zero-based offset.

### Flags

| Flag                          | Required | Description                                                             |
| ----------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--api-version=<value>`       | no       | Override the api version used for api requests made by this command     |
| `--component-type=<value>`    | yes      | Required supported component type used to filter available components.  |
| `--data-kit=<value>`          | yes      | Required data-kit developer name whose available components are listed. |
| `--flags-dir=<value>`         | no       | Import flag values from a directory.                                    |
| `--json`                      | no       | Format output as json.                                                  |
| `--limit=<value>`             | no       | Maximum components to return, from 1 through 200.                       |
| `--offset=<value>`            | no       | Number of components to skip before returning results.                  |
| `--target-org=<value>` (`-o`) | yes      | Username or alias of the target org.                                    |
| `--timing`                    | no       | Write request timing details to stderr.                                 |

### Examples

- List Data Lake Objects available to a specific data kit:

  ```shell
  sf data360 data-kit available --target-org my-org --component-type DataLakeObject --data-kit CustomerFoundation --offset 0
  ```

- List the next page of data streams available to the same data kit:

  ```shell
  sf data360 data-kit available --target-org my-org --component-type DataStream --data-kit CustomerFoundation --limit 50 --offset 50
  ```

## `sf data360 data-kit deploy`

Deploy components from a Data 360 data kit.

Submit a JSON `components` array with the required `asyncMode=true` query parameter. Each component's `config` object is specific to its component type. The Connect API can return a job ID but defines no deployment-job status endpoint; inspect each submitted component with `data-kit component status`.

### Flags

| Flag                          | Required | Description                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--api-version=<value>`       | no       | Override the api version used for api requests made by this command                                 |
| `--data-space=<value>`        | no       | Data space to use.                                                                                  |
| `--file=<value>` (`-f`)       | yes      | Path to a JSON object containing the component deployment `components` array, or `-` to read stdin. |
| `--flags-dir=<value>`         | no       | Import flag values from a directory.                                                                |
| `--json`                      | no       | Format output as json.                                                                              |
| `--name=<value>` (`-n`)       | yes      | Developer name of the data kit containing the components.                                           |
| `--target-org=<value>` (`-o`) | yes      | Username or alias of the target org.                                                                |
| `--timing`                    | no       | Write request timing details to stderr.                                                             |

### Examples

- Deploy selected components to the default data space:

  ```shell
  sf data360 data-kit deploy --target-org my-org --name CustomerFoundation --file examples/data-kit/deploy.json
  ```

- Deploy selected components to another data space:

  ```shell
  sf data360 data-kit deploy --target-org my-org --name CustomerFoundation --file examples/data-kit/deploy.json --data-space loyalty
  ```

List Data 360 data kits.

List data kits from `GET /ssot/data-kits`, optionally filtered by package namespace. This API has no get-single operation; use `data-kit manifest` when you need a kit's member metadata.

| `--json`                      | no       | Format output as json.                                              |
| `--namespace=<value>`         | no       | Namespace prefix used to filter data kits.                          |
| `--target-org=<value>` (`-o`) | yes      | Username or alias of the target org.                                |
| `--timing`                    | no       | Write request timing details to stderr.                             |

### Examples

- List all visible data kits:

  ```shell
  sf data360 data-kit list --target-org my-org
  ```

- Filter data kits by namespace:

  ```shell
  sf data360 data-kit list --target-org my-org --namespace acme
  ```

## `sf data360 data-kit undeploy`

Undeploy components from a Data 360 data kit.

Submit an ordered JSON `components` array of component `type` and `name` values with `asyncMode=true`. This destructive operation can return a job ID but has no deployment-job status endpoint; inspect each submitted component with `data-kit component status`.

### Flags

| Flag                          | Required | Description                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--api-version=<value>`       | no       | Override the api version used for api requests made by this command                                           |
| `--data-space=<value>`        | no       | Data space to use.                                                                                            |
| `--file=<value>` (`-f`)       | yes      | Path to a JSON object containing the ordered component undeployment `components` array, or `-` to read stdin. |
| `--flags-dir=<value>`         | no       | Import flag values from a directory.                                                                          |
| `--json`                      | no       | Format output as json.                                                                                        |
| `--name=<value>` (`-n`)       | yes      | Developer name of the data kit containing the components.                                                     |
| `--no-prompt`                 | no       | Do not prompt for confirmation.                                                                               |
| `--target-org=<value>` (`-o`) | yes      | Username or alias of the target org.                                                                          |
| `--timing`                    | no       | Write request timing details to stderr.                                                                       |

### Examples

- Review component undeployment interactively:

  ```shell
  sf data360 data-kit undeploy --target-org my-org --name CustomerFoundation --file examples/data-kit/undeploy.json
  ```

- Undeploy components in a noninteractive script:

  ```shell
  sf data360 data-kit undeploy --target-org my-org --name CustomerFoundation --file examples/data-kit/undeploy.json --data-space loyalty --no-prompt
  ```

## `sf data360 data-kit update`

Synchronize components in a Data 360 data kit.

Replace a data kit's component set with the `components` array in a JSON definition. This PATCH operation is destructive: components omitted from the definition are removed from the kit.

### Flags

| Flag                          | Required | Description                                                                  |
| ----------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--api-version=<value>`       | no       | Override the api version used for api requests made by this command          |
| `--file=<value>` (`-f`)       | yes      | Path to the replacement component-set JSON definition, or `-` to read stdin. |
| `--flags-dir=<value>`         | no       | Import flag values from a directory.                                         |
| `--json`                      | no       | Format output as json.                                                       |
| `--name=<value>` (`-n`)       | yes      | Developer name of the data kit to synchronize.                               |
| `--no-prompt`                 | no       | Do not prompt for confirmation.                                              |
| `--target-org=<value>` (`-o`) | yes      | Username or alias of the target org.                                         |
| `--timing`                    | no       | Write request timing details to stderr.                                      |

### Examples

- Review the destructive sync interactively:

  ```shell
  sf data360 data-kit update --target-org my-org --name CustomerFoundation --file examples/data-kit/components.json
  ```

- Synchronize components in a noninteractive script:

  ```shell
  sf data360 data-kit update --target-org my-org --name CustomerFoundation --file examples/data-kit/components.json --no-prompt
  ```

## `sf data360 ingest`

Stream records into Data 360.

### Flags

| Flag                           | Required | Description                                                         |

| `--flags-dir=<value>`          | no       | Import flag values from a directory.                                |
| `--json`                       | no       | Format output as json.                                              |
| `--no-prompt`                  | no       | Do not prompt for confirmation.                                     |
| `--object-name=<value>`        | yes      | Object configured for the ingestion connector.                      |
| `--source-name=<value>` (`-s`) | yes      | Ingestion API connector name.                                       |

### Examples

  ```shell
  sf data360 ingest --target-org my-org --source-name connector --object-name Contact --file contacts.ndjson
  ```

  ```shell
  sf data360 ingest --target-org my-org --source-name connector --object-name Contact < contacts.json
  ```

## `sf data360 ingest bulk`

Bulk ingest CSV files into Data 360.

Confirm the billable upsert or delete, create a bulk job, upload CSV batches below 150 MB, close it, and optionally wait.

### Flags

| Flag                           | Required | Description                                                         |
| ------------------------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--api-version=<value>`        | no       | Override the api version used for api requests made by this command |
| `--async`                      | no       | Return immediately after submitting the operation.                  |
| `--file=<value>` (`-f`)        | yes      | CSV input file; repeat for multiple files.                          |
| `--flags-dir=<value>`          | no       | Import flag values from a directory.                                |
| `--json`                       | no       | Format output as json.                                              |
| `--no-prompt`                  | no       | Do not prompt for confirmation.                                     |
| `--object-name=<value>`        | yes      | Object configured for the ingestion connector.                      |
| `--operation=<value>`          | no       | Bulk operation: `upsert` or `delete`.                               |
| `--source-name=<value>` (`-s`) | yes      | Ingestion API connector name.                                       |
| `--target-org=<value>` (`-o`)  | yes      | Username or alias of the target org.                                |
| `--timing`                     | no       | Write request timing details to stderr.                             |
| `--wait=<value>` (`-w`)        | no       | Minutes to wait for ingestion completion.                           |

### Examples

- Upload and wait for completion:

  ```shell
  sf data360 ingest bulk --target-org my-org --source-name connector --object-name Contact --file contacts.csv --wait 10
  ```

- Upload multiple delete files asynchronously:

  ```shell
  sf data360 ingest bulk --target-org my-org --source-name connector --object-name Contact --file a.csv --file b.csv --operation delete --async
  ```

## `sf data360 query`

Run SQL against Data 360.

Submit SQL to the Data 360 Query SQL API, or start the interactive REPL when no query source is provided in a TTY.

### Flags

| Flag                           | Required | Description                                                         |
| ------------------------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--api-version=<value>`        | no       | Override the api version used for api requests made by this command |
| `--async`                      | no       | Return immediately after submitting the operation.                  |
| `--data-space=<value>`         | no       | Data space to use.                                                  |
| `--file=<value>` (`-f`)        | no       | SQL input file path, or - to read from stdin.                       |
| `--flags-dir=<value>`          | no       | Import flag values from a directory.                                |
| `--json`                       | no       | Format output as json.                                              |
| `--no-prompt`                  | no       | Do not prompt for confirmation.                                     |
| `--output-file=<value>`        | no       | Write result data to a file.                                        |
| `--query=<value>` (`-q`)       | no       | SQL text to execute.                                                |
| `--query-options-file=<value>` | no       | JSON file containing Query SQL `sqlParameters` and `querySettings`. |
| `--result-format=<value>`      | no       | Format emitted result data.                                         |
| `--row-limit=<value>`          | no       | Maximum rows to request.                                            |
| `--target-org=<value>` (`-o`)  | yes      | Username or alias of the target org.                                |
| `--timing`                     | no       | Write request timing details to stderr.                             |
| `--wait=<value>` (`-w`)        | no       | Minutes to wait for query completion.                               |
| `--workload-name=<value>`      | no       | Scenario name added to Data 360 query logs for support diagnostics. |

### Examples

- Run an inline query and display a table:

  ```shell
  sf data360 query --query 'SELECT * FROM "ssot__Individual__dlm" LIMIT 10' --target-org my-org
  ```

- Pipe SQL and write RFC-4180 CSV:

  ```shell
  sf data360 query --file - --result-format csv --output-file rows.csv --target-org my-org < query.sql
  ```

- Submit asynchronously and resume later:

  ```shell
  sf data360 query --query 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "ssot__Individual__dlm"' --async --target-org my-org
  ```

- Run parameterized SQL with support-visible workload metadata and execution settings:

  ```shell
  sf data360 query --query 'SELECT * FROM "FlightSeat__dll" WHERE "boardingstatus__c" = :status' --query-options-file query-options.json --workload-name nightly-seat-audit --target-org my-org
  ```

- Start the interactive SQL REPL with persistent history:

  ```shell
  sf data360 query --target-org my-org
  ```

| ----------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |

## `sf data360 query hybrid`

Run hybrid search through Data 360 SQL.

Builds hybrid_search SQL and executes the standard cached query lifecycle through the Connect
`query-sql` endpoint, which accepts Data 360 SQL. Salesforce's published Data 360 SQL reference does
not currently document this generated hybrid_search form. Treat the command as beta and validate its
SQL against a non-production target org before relying on it; the generated dialect has not completed
live verification.

### Flags

| Flag                          | Required | Description                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--api-version=<value>`       | no       | Override the api version used for api requests made by this command |
| `--async`                     | no       | Return immediately after submitting the operation.                  |
| `--data-space=<value>`        | no       | Data space to use.                                                  |
| `--filter=<value>`            | no       | Search prefilter expression.                                        |
| `--flags-dir=<value>`         | no       | Import flag values from a directory.                                |
| `--index=<value>`             | yes      | Search index base or full index table name.                         |
| `--json`                      | no       | Format output as json.                                              |
| `--no-prompt`                 | no       | Do not prompt for confirmation.                                     |
| `--output-file=<value>`       | no       | Write result data to a file.                                        |
| `--result-format=<value>`     | no       | Format emitted result data.                                         |
| `--select=<value>`            | no       | Comma-separated chunk fields to select.                             |
| `--target-org=<value>` (`-o`) | yes      | Username or alias of the target org.                                |
| `--text=<value>` (`-t`)       | yes      | Natural language search text.                                       |
| `--timing`                    | no       | Write request timing details to stderr.                             |
| `--top-k=<value>`             | no       | Maximum matches.                                                    |
| `--wait=<value>` (`-w`)       | no       | Minutes to wait for query completion.                               |

### Examples

- Search an index:

  ```shell

- Add a prefilter:

  ```

## `sf data360 setup eca`

Create an External Client Application (ECA) for Data 360 Direct API access.

Provisions an External Client Application on the target org with the OAuth scopes required by Data 360 Direct Query, Profile, and Ingestion APIs.

The command creates the ECA via the Metadata SOAP API, configures its OAuth settings with the required `cdp_*` scopes, and retrieves the resulting consumer key. After the ECA is active, reauthorize the org with the consumer key and scopes to enable Direct API access.

The Metadata API approach is the Salesforce-endorsed mechanism for programmatic ECA creation and is documented on Trailhead.

### Flags

| Flag                             | Required | Description                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--api-version=<value>`          | no       | Override the api version used for api requests made by this command                                            |
| `--app-name=<value>` (`-n`)      | no       | Developer name for the External Client Application (alphanumeric and underscores only; maximum 30 characters). |
| `--contact-email=<value>` (`-e`) | no       | Contact email registered with the External Client Application (defaults to the authenticated username).        |
| `--flags-dir=<value>`            | no       | Import flag values from a directory.                                                                           |
| `--json`                         | no       | Format output as json.                                                                                         |
| `--no-prompt`                    | no       | Do not prompt for confirmation.                                                                                |
| `--target-org=<value>` (`-o`)    | yes      | Username or alias of the target org.                                                                           |
| `--timing`                       | no       | Write request timing details to stderr.                                                                        |

### Examples

- Create an ECA on the default target org:

  ```shell
  sf data360 setup eca --target-org my-org
  ```

- Create an ECA with a custom app name:

  ```shell
  sf data360 setup eca --target-org my-org --app-name MyDataCloudCLI
  ```

- Create without interactive confirmation:

  ```shell
  sf data360 setup eca --target-org my-org --no-prompt --json
  ```

| `--name=<value>` (`-n`)       | yes      | Resource developer name, display name, or ID.                       |
| `--target-org=<value>` (`-o`) | yes      | Username or alias of the target org.                                |
| `--timing`                    | no       | Write request timing details to stderr.                             |

### Examples

- Run against an org:

  ```shell
  sf data360 transform update --target-org my-org --name Example --file -
  ```

- Return JSON:

  ```shell
  sf data360 transform update --target-org my-org --name Example --file - --json
  ```

## `sf data360 transform validate`

Validate data transforms.

### Flags

| `--name=<value>` (`-n`)       | yes      | Resource developer name, display name, or ID.                       |
| `--target-org=<value>` (`-o`) | yes      | Username or alias of the target org.                                |
| `--timing`                    | no       | Write request timing details to stderr.                             |

### Examples
